title: Modified Sgarbossa Criteria
sources: Sgarbossa EB et al. NEJM 1996; Smith SW et al. Ann Emerg Med 2012 (modified — replaces the ≥ 5 mm discordance rule with the ST/S ratio)
purpose: Identifies acute coronary occlusion (STEMI-equivalent / OMI) in the presence of left bundle branch block or a ventricular paced rhythm, where the standard ST-elevation criteria don't apply. ANY positive criterion is a positive test.

items.label: Concordant ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in ≥ 1 lead (ST segment and QRS in the SAME direction)
Concordant ST depression ≥ 1 mm in ≥ 1 of leads V1–V3
Proportionally excessive discordant ST elevation — ST/S ratio ≤ −0.25 in ≥ 1 lead with ≥ 1 mm STE (ST elevation ≥ 25% of the depth of the preceding S wave)

interpretation.label: Negative — no Sgarbossa criterion met. Does NOT rule out occlusion — reassess with serial ECGs, the clinical picture, troponin, and echo; a hyperacute or evolving pattern can still warrant the cath lab
POSITIVE — treat as a STEMI-equivalent. Activate the cath lab / thrombolysis pathway per your local ACS protocol

notes: The modified (Smith) version replaces the original third criterion (≥ 5 mm absolute discordant STE) with the ST/S ratio ≤ −0.25, which markedly improves sensitivity while keeping specificity. Measure the ST segment and S/R wave at the J point relative to the PR / TP baseline. Also applies to paced rhythms (with slightly lower performance).
